compiled_state.description:
## The file

`src/rebar/signing.py` is **800 LOC against the 800 hard cap** — re-measured on `origin/main`
@ `09abac96` (2026-08-19). ZERO headroom: any edit at all now fails the CI module-size gate.
(Filed at 798; it grew two lines since — exactly the failure mode this ticket ends. Gerrit
change 1916 failed today when a six-line comment pushed a 798-line file to 804.)

Deferred from `cinderlike-lucky-akitainu` because this cut cannot be made without editing a test.

## Concern map (re-measured on origin/main @ 09abac96)

| concern | LOC | symbols |
|---|---|---|
| A manifest vocabulary + gate provenance | ~200 | `SigningError`, `parse_manifest`, `VERIFIED_AT_SHA_PREFIX`, `verified_at_sha_step`, `verified_at_sha_from_manifest`, `verified_at_sha_subject`, `REBAR_VERSION_PREFIX`, `rebar_version_step`, `rebar_version_from_manifest`, `_gate_source_dir`, `_baked_commit_sha`, `_gate_commit_sha`, `gate_code_version`, `head_sha` |
| B legacy symmetric HMAC scheme | ~260 | `ALGORITHM`, `PAYLOAD_VERSION`, `_NO_KEY`, `signing_key`, `_generate_key_file`, `key_fingerprint`, `_canonical_payload`, `compute_signature`, `verify_record`, `_hmac_opcert_not_certified` |
| C attestation dispatch + persistence + CLI arms (stays) | ~370 | `OPCERT_KINDS`, `verify_attestation_record`, `_sign_manifest_under_lock`, `sign_manifest`, `_resolve_and_reduce`, `most_recent_attestation`, `_record_for_kind`, `verify_signature`, `verify_attestations`, `sign_cli`, `verify_signature_cli` |

## Design

Two cuts along the call-graph seams that already exist, producing **sibling modules, not a
package** (the cap is per-file either way, and `_opcert_signing.py` — split out of this same
module in story 8d8e — is the established precedent):

- `_signing_manifest.py` (A) — the vocabulary layer: error type, manifest validation, the two
  signed-step vocabularies (`verified-at-sha:`, `rebar-version:`), and the git/build provenance
  producing the `rebar-version:` value. A pure leaf: stdlib only, no rebar imports.
- `_signing_hmac.py` (B) — the retired symmetric scheme kept whole: key custody,
  canonicalisation, `compute_signature`, the `verify_record` verdict. Imports A only.
- `signing.py` (C) — stays the entry module: scheme dispatch (`verify_attestation_record`), the
  op-cert sign path, the resolve/reduce read path, the two CLI arms. Re-exports the moved
  surface so `rebar.signing` remains the single import point.

Import direction `signing -> _signing_hmac -> _signing_manifest`, acyclic; no back-edges.

**The CLI arms are NOT cut** though they are a genuine seam: `_signing_cli.py` would be ~105 LOC
— above the 100 floor but below the 200-500 target band — and `signing.py` at ~370 already has
~430 lines of margin. Recorded so the next person knows the cut is pre-analysed. If ever taken,
the arms must reach `sign_manifest` / `verify_signature` through the module attribute
(`from rebar import signing` in-function), never `from rebar.signing import X` at module level,
or the eight `verify_signature` and one `sign_manifest` monkeypatches bind pre-patch and no-op.

## The monkeypatch hazard — why this needs a test edit

`_baked_commit_sha` is monkeypatched **on the `signing` module** at
`tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py:141,153,164`, and its only consumer `_gate_commit_sha`
calls it as a BARE GLOBAL (`signing.py:308,312`). Move both into `_signing_manifest.py` and
`_gate_commit_sha` resolves `_baked_commit_sha` from `_signing_manifest.__dict__`, so a patch on
`signing` becomes a NO-OP. Two of the three tests fail loudly. The third (`:164`,
`assert "STALEBAKED" not in got`) passes **VACUOUSLY** — it silently stops testing the
live-over-baked precedence it was written to prove. That third one is the dangerous one.

**Chosen remedy: (1) re-point the three patches at `rebar._signing_manifest`** — legitimate
re-anchoring to the new structure, not a relaxed assertion; the symbol is private with zero
`src/` consumers outside the family. Rejected: keeping the 69-LOC provenance sub-family in
`signing.py` (splits one concern across two modules for no gain), and an in-function
`from rebar.signing import _baked_commit_sha` back-edge (a cycle).

**The vacuous-pass class is closed structurally, not by inspection.** A new guard test asserts
POSITIVELY that a patch on `_baked_commit_sha` is observed by `_gate_commit_sha`
(`_gate_commit_sha(source_dir=<non-git dir>) == "<sentinel>"`). If the two ever land in
different modules again, that guard fails loudly instead of the precedence test going quiet.
The `:164` assertion is additionally strengthened from a negative (`"STALEBAKED" not in got`) to
a positive one pinning the live short SHA, so it cannot pass without the precedence holding.

## Other constraints found (verified on this commit)

- Re-export surface measured, not guessed: 34 distinct `signing.<attr>` attribute uses plus 9
  `from rebar.signing import` names across `src/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`. EVERY moved symbol is
  re-exported and listed in `__all__` (ruff F401 would otherwise flag them; `__all__` documents
  the contract).
- `docs/reuse-surface.md` documents `sign_manifest`, `verify_signature`, `verify_attestations`,
  `verify_record`, `head_sha`; `tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py` introspects NINE
  `signing.*` callables with `inspect.signature`. Six of the nine move — the re-export must carry
  them with unchanged parameter lists. That test is the CI tripwire.
- Six PRIVATE names must be re-exported despite the underscore: `_gate_commit_sha` (imported by
  `llm/build_drift.py:127`), `_baked_commit_sha`, `_NO_KEY`, `_generate_key_file`,
  `_canonical_payload`, `_hmac_opcert_not_certified`.
- **Silent-behaviour change to state in the commit:** `verify_record` and
  `_hmac_opcert_not_certified` call `verified_at_sha_from_manifest` / `rebar_version_from_manifest`
  as bare globals; after the cut those resolve in `_signing_hmac`'s globals, so a patch on
  `signing` no longer reaches them. Audited: the one test patching
  `signing.verified_at_sha_from_manifest` (`test_plan_review_drift_floor.py:190`) also stubs
  `signing.verify_signature`, so `verify_record` is never reached. Rule going forward:
  **patch a moved symbol in the module that DEFINES it.**
- The 21 `rebar.signing.head_sha` monkeypatches are unaffected: every consumer reaches it through
  the module attribute or an in-function `from rebar.signing import head_sha` (both resolve at
  call time against the patched `signing.__dict__`), and `signing.py` itself no longer calls it.
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` has ZERO keys for `signing.py` — the ratchet is not a
  constraint here. `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is NOT touched (it is locked; a contributor
  change to it fails CI).

## Portability

No CI-provider coupling. The module-size rule is enforced in-process by
`tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` (via `tests/module_size_support.py`, the single source
the GitHub Actions gate also reads), so the constraint holds under any CI provider or none —
`make test` alone catches a regression. Nothing added here triggers on a specific CI system.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/signing.py` <= 500 LOC with real headroom (target ~370, >= 200 lines of margin
      below the 800 cap); every new module in [100, 500] and ideally [200, 500].
- [ ] All nine `signing.*` callables in `test_reuse_surface_doc.py` reachable with UNCHANGED
      parameter lists; the six private names re-exported; `docs/reuse-surface.md` unchanged
      (the surface does not move).
- [ ] The `_baked_commit_sha` hazard resolved by remedy (1), and the `:164` vacuous-pass risk
      closed by a POSITIVE guard test rather than left latent.
- [ ] Import graph acyclic: `signing -> _signing_hmac -> _signing_manifest`, no back-edges.
- [ ] Full-suite test-count parity (no test silently dropped); `make lint`, `make typecheck`,
      and `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` green.
